chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who examines a slave woman in order to buy her. He said: “There is no harm in looking at her attractive features and touching her, so long as he does not look at what is not appropriate for him to look at.”

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permitted
key_terms.لِيَشْتَرِيَهَا: for the purpose of buying her
key_terms.مَا لَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُ النَّظَرُ إِلَيْه: that which is not appropriate or lawful for him to look at
key_terms.يَعْتَرِضُ الْأَمَةَ: examines a slave woman presented for purchase

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on looking at and touching a slave woman before purchasing her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about examining a female slave before purchase. It permits looking at her attractive features and touching her for assessment, while setting a limit that one must not look at what is impermissible to view.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4976 - Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir, who said:
"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who examines a slave woman to purchase her.
Imam (as) said: 'There is no harm in looking at her attractive features and touching her, as long as he does not look at what is not appropriate for him to see.'"
